traps: Text Classification (文本分类) = NLU (NOT NLG)

"AI relies only on fixed rules" → False

sections.title: ⭐⭐ Knowledge Representation (知识表示) — Comparison
content: Document (文档) | Raw/semi-structured text

sections.title: ⭐⭐ Turing Test (图灵测试, 1950)
content: Human evaluator interacts via text with one human + one machine
If evaluator cannot distinguish → machine passes

content: Requirements → Data collection → Preprocessing → Feature extraction → Model building → Evaluation → Deployment → Iterate

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ Stemming vs Lemmatization (词干提取 vs 词元化)
traps: helped/helps→help = Stemming (suffix removal -ed, -s)
was/am/is→be = Lemmatization (dictionary knowledge for irregular forms)
Poetry Analysis: do NOT stem/lemmatize (rhyme/rhythm crucial)
SpaCy has NO Stemming; NLTK has both

traps: \b\w+[-]\w+\b → compound words (high-tech), NOT words ending with hyphen
[a-zA-Z]\w*d+ → multiple matches, not just 'and'
s[0]=first, s[-1]=last; vowel check: s[0].lower() in 'aeiou' and s[-1].lower() in 'aeiou'

weeks.title: Text Vectorization (文本向量化) & Similarity (相似度)

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ BOW (Bag-of-Words, 词袋模型)

rows: Ignores context & word order (忽略上下文和词序)
Works for text classification & IR (适合分类和检索)
High-dimensional feature space (高维特征空间)
Lack of semantic info (缺乏语义)

content: BOW word order loss: 'John is quicker than Mary' = 'Mary is quicker than John' → same vector!

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ N-gram (N元组)

rows: Captures partial context/word order (捕获部分上下文)
Sparsity (稀疏性) — vocab grows as Vⁿ
Ignores overall structure/meaning (忽略整体语义)
Choice of N is hard (N的选择困难)

content: Unigram='I','am','learning','NLP' | Bigram='am learning','learning NLP' | Trigram='am learning NLP'

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency, 词频-逆文档频率) — Formulas
formulas: TF(t,d) = count(t in d) / total words in d
content: Word in every doc: IDF=log(1)=0 → zero weight
Word in 1 doc: IDF=log(N) → highest weight
Why log: compress extreme values to manageable range

rows: Miss word relationships (缺失词间关系)
Lack of semantic understanding (缺乏语义理解)
Not suited for small corpora (不适合小语料库)

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ CountVectorizer vs TfidfVectorizer (计数向量器 vs TF-IDF向量器)
content: CountVec: doc1('hot sun') & doc3('hot encoding') most similar (0.408) — misleading!
TF-IDF: doc2('chocolate milk') & doc4('latte milk') most similar (0.232) — smarter!
ngram_range=(1,2) | Unigrams + bigrams
Vector dim | Total n-grams in vocabulary
traps: Corpus with (1,2)-gram produces 8+ features, NOT 7

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ Traditional Methods Comparison (传统方法总对比)
traps: BOW IGNORES word order
TF-IDF does NOT consider context/semantic relationships
TF-IDF = high-dim sparse; DL prefers low-dim dense

sections.title: ⭐⭐ VSM (Vector Space Model, 向量空间模型)

rows: Text → points in vector space; similar words nearby
Encoding text as integers → feature vectors
Each word → binary vector, only one 1, rest 0

traps: Proposed [d2,d1000,d3,d1,d9] is False — d1 and d9 swapped

traps: Hypernym/Hyponym = IS-A | Meronym/Holonym = PART-OF — don't confuse!
content: Limitations: limited coverage, static, not computational, domain-specific, manual curation

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ Word Embedding Fundamentals (词嵌入基础)
content: Distributional Hypothesis (分布假说): similar contexts → similar meanings
Word Embedding: dense low-dim vector (d=50-300)
Self-Supervised Learning (自监督学习): no manual labels
Word Analogy: king-man+woman≈queen; e_boy-e_girl≈e_brother-e_sister
traps: 1000-word vocab → 1000-dim embedding? → False (typical 50-300)
"Modern NLP doesn't use embeddings" → False (W2V→GloVe→BERT→GPT all use)

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ TF-IDF vs Word Embeddings (TF-IDF vs 词嵌入)
content: 1 | High-dimensional representation (高维表示)
2 | Sparse (稀疏)
3 | OOV words (未登录词)
4 | Lack of semantic meaning (缺乏语义含义)
5 | → Poor performance on majority of NLP tasks

content: Gensim default: vector_size=100

content: 1. Target+context = positive | 2. Random words = negative
3. Logistic regression classifier | 4. Weights = embeddings
Reduces softmax O(V) → binary O(k)

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ N-gram LM (N-gram Language Model, N元语言模型)
content: Markov Assumption: only previous n-1 words
Limitations: sparsity, fixed window, no semantics
traps: "N-gram uses deep semantic reasoning" → False (statistical only)
Bigram P(happy|feel) = 40/100 = 0.4; Count(happy)=30 is DISTRACTOR

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ RNN (Recurrent Neural Network, 循环神经网络)
formulas: J = -(1/T) Σ log P(correct word at t)
content: Stateful computation: hₜ carries info across time steps
Parameter sharing: same Wₕ, Wₑ at every step
BPTT: error propagates backward through time

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ FFNN (Feed-Forward NN, 前馈神经网络) vs RNN
⭐⭐⭐ Gradient Problems (梯度问题)
content: Example | "she tried to print her tickets... installed toner... finally printed her ___"
Problem | RNN needs to connect 'tickets' (early) to prediction (end) — signal lost
Math | Gradients multiply by Wₕ at each step: if |Wₕ|<1 → exponential shrinkage

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory, 长短期记忆网络)
content: Dual state: hₜ (short-term) + cₜ (long-term cell state)
Cell update uses ADDITION (not multiplication) → gradient flows
traps: "More layers auto-prevent vanishing gradient" → ❌ (key=gating)
"LSTM replaces recurrent with feedforward" → ❌ (still recurrent)
"LSTM removes backpropagation" → ❌ (still uses BPTT)

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ PPL (Perplexity, 困惑度) & LR (Learning Rate, 学习率)
content: PPL: low=good prediction, high=confused
traps: "Low LR → faster training" → False (OPPOSITE!)

Basic building block of neural networks

rows: 'terribly exciting' — forward sees 'terribly'→negative? Need right context 'exciting'→positive!
Uses vector as init state, autoregressive generation

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ Seq2Seq Training vs Testing (训练 vs 测试)
traps: Exposure Bias (曝光偏差): model never sees its own errors during training → fragile at test time

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ Attention (注意力机制) — Definition & Steps

rows: Attention = weighted average over a set of inputs
Compute pairwise similarity: each encoder state vs decoder state
Compute weighted average of encoder hidden states

content: 1. score_i = dot(decoder_state, encoder_state_i)
2. α = softmax(scores) → attention distribution
3. context = Σαᵢ × encoder_state_i → attention output
4. [decoder_state ; context] → concat → prediction

examples.label: Translation: 'il a m' entarté' → 'he hit me with a pie'

sections.title: ⭐⭐⭐ Seq2Seq vs Seq2Seq+Attention (对比)
content: Problem | Single fixed-length vector must capture ALL source info
Effect | Long sentences → information loss
Solution | → Attention mechanism

rows: 'Attention Is All You Need' (Vaswani et al.)
Each word attends to ALL words, fully parallel
Multi-Head Attention, FFN, LayerNorm, Residual Connections
